info.title: GazeLens API
info.description: Webcam gaze estimation and multi-agent UX evaluation.

get.description: Which ui_page values a test_ui session can use.

post.description: Create a session and resolve the element layout it will be scored against.

get.description: This user's sessions, newest first. Never anyone else's.

post.description:
Attach a completed calibration session and fit its gaze model.

The calibration itself is collected by backend/calibration's own
endpoints; this only links the result to a session and triggers training,
so the two modules stay independently usable.

Append a batch of estimated gaze points to the session's stream.

Batched rather than one request per frame: at 30Hz that would be 1800
requests a minute per participant. Invalid points should be included --
backend/attribution needs the gaps.
Run the analysis chain. Returns immediately; poll the session or report.

get.description:
The report, or 202 + status while the pipeline is still running.

202 rather than 404 for a pending report: the resource will exist, and a
404 would tell a polling dashboard to give up.
The target grids, so the client renders exactly what the server scores.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api Calibration Sessions Get

post.description: Open a session and hand back the full target sequence.
Run a burst of frames through the pupil detector and store the hits.

Close the session and write the training export.

Completing a poor calibration is allowed -- it is saved with
ready_for_regression=False rather than refused. Throwing away a
participant's data because coverage came out at 70% would be worse than
keeping it clearly labelled.

Fit a per-session gaze model from that session's calibration data.

Per session, per sitting: the pupil-to-screen mapping depends on head
position, seating distance, lighting and camera angle, none of which
survive a change of participant or setup.

The body is optional -- training with no arguments is the common case.
Defaulted here rather than in the signature: a `TrainRequest()` default
would build one instance at import time and share it across every request,
which is a mutable process-wide object masquerading as a per-call default.

schema.title: Response List Trained Models Api Gaze Models Get

get.description: A trained model's stored accuracy, without retraining it.

post.description: One frame's pupil positions -> one screen coordinate.

A burst of frames -> a slice of the gaze stream.

Invalid frames are returned in place rather than dropped, so the caller
can see where the gaps are -- a missing frame silently removed would read
downstream as continuous attention.

get.description:
The thresholds a result was produced under.

Exposed because every number this module emits depends on them, and a
metric quoted without its threshold isn't reproducible.

Screenshot a URL and detect its elements.

get.description:
Liveness, plus whether live capture can actually run on this machine.

cv_available is False on a clean clone (models/*.pt is gitignored).
Surfacing it here beats finding out from a 500 on the first frame.

CalibrationLinkRequest.title: CalibrationLinkRequest
CalibrationLinkRequest.description: Attach a completed calibration session and train its gaze model.

CalibrationPointModel.title: CalibrationPointModel
CalibrationPointModel.description: One on-screen target, normalised to [0, 1] of the viewport.

CreateSessionRequest.title: CreateSessionRequest
CreateSessionRequest.description:
Start a session.

mode="test_ui" needs ui_page; mode="url" needs target_url. Enforced here
rather than in the route so an invalid combination is a 422 with a field
path, not a 500 three modules deep.

DefaultsResponse.title: DefaultsResponse
DefaultsResponse.description: The thresholds in force, so a client isn't guessing what produced a number.

DiagnosticsModel.title: DiagnosticsModel
DiagnosticsModel.description:
Things worth knowing that SessionMetrics has no field for.

SessionMetrics is a fixed contract owned by backend/agents; it must not
grow, so these live alongside it rather than inside it.

ElementInput.title: ElementInput
ElementInput.description:
One UI element: where it is, and what it means.

Accepts either a normalised (x, y, w, h) tuple -- the form
backend/reports/heatmap_stub.py already uses -- or explicit x/y/width/
height, which is what Playwright's boundingBox() returns and therefore
what backend/render most likely produces. Pixel values need `viewport`
on the request to normalise against.

ErrorMetrics.title: ErrorMetrics
ErrorMetrics.description:
Held-out accuracy. `validation` states how it was measured.

Degrees fields are absent unless viewing distance + screen size were
supplied on the request; `degrees_unavailable` explains why when so.

EstimateBatchRequest.title: EstimateBatchRequest
EstimateBatchRequest.description:
A burst of frames. Frames with no pupil are allowed here -- they come
back as invalid GazePoints, preserving the gap in the stream.

smoothing.title: Smoothing
smoothing.description: EMA factor for a live cursor. Leave at 0 for the raw stream attribution consumes.

PatternsResponse.title: PatternsResponse
PatternsResponse.description:
GET /api/calibration/patterns -- lets the client render the same grid
the server will score against, instead of hardcoding it twice.

PupilInput.title: PupilInput
PupilInput.description:
One eye's pupil centre, normalised WITHIN its eye box ([0,1]).

These are `x_eye`/`y_eye` from a cv.PupilDetection -- not frame
coordinates. Sending frame coordinates would be silently wrong rather
than an error, so it's worth being explicit: the model was trained on
eye-box coordinates and will produce nonsense from anything else.

PupilReading.title: PupilReading
PupilReading.description: Echoed back per eye so the client can draw a live preview dot.

ReportPendingResponse.title: ReportPendingResponse
ReportPendingResponse.description: Returned with 202 while the pipeline hasn't produced a report yet.

ReportResponse.title: ReportResponse
ReportResponse.description:
The agent chain's output, unreshaped.

`pipeline_result` is exactly what agents/orchestrator.run_pipeline()
returned -- behavior_summary, issues, recommendations_kept,
recommendations_rejected. Not flattened or renamed: backend/reports
already consumes that shape, and a second shape here would be one more
thing to keep in sync for no gain.

SessionDetailResponse.title: SessionDetailResponse
SessionDetailResponse.description: One session, plus the state of the modules it depends on.

SessionListResponse.title: SessionListResponse
SessionListResponse.description: Paginated, because the dashboard lists every session a user ever ran.

SessionMetricsModel.title: SessionMetricsModel
SessionMetricsModel.description:
Mirrors backend/agents/schemas.py SessionMetrics exactly.

`ttff` deliberately omits elements that were never fixated -- see
metrics.py. It is not a bug that its key set can be smaller than
dwell_time's.

SubmitSamplesRequest.title: SubmitSamplesRequest
SubmitSamplesRequest.description:
A burst of frames captured while one target was on screen.

Frames are base64 (a raw string or a full `data:image/jpeg;base64,...`
data URL -- canvas.toDataURL() output can be posted as-is).

A burst rather than one frame per request: the client holds each target
for roughly a second, and batching that fixation into a single POST
keeps the round-trip count down and guarantees every frame in the batch
really did belong to the same target.

min_confidence.title: Min Confidence
min_confidence.description: Drop calibration rows whose detector confidence is below this.

viewing_distance_cm.title: Viewing Distance Cm
viewing_distance_cm.description: Eye-to-screen distance. Supply with screen_diagonal_in to get degrees.

TrainRequest.title: TrainRequest
TrainRequest.description:
Train a gaze model from a stored calibration session.

All fields optional: the default path is "train session X with whatever
backend/calibration stored for it, and pick the model yourself".

api__schemas__GazePointInput.title: GazePointInput
api__schemas__GazePointInput.description:
One estimated gaze point, normalised [0,1] screen coordinates.

Matches the GazePoint that backend/gaze_estimation emits. Invalid points
(blinks) should be SENT, not filtered -- backend/attribution needs the gap
to distinguish a blink from a glance away.

attribution__schemas__GazePointInput.title: GazePointInput
attribution__schemas__GazePointInput.description:
One raw gaze point.

Matches the GazePoint shape backend/gaze_estimation emits, but is declared
independently -- attribution must not depend on that module.
